## Keepalive false-kill pattern: load storm vs dead service (2026-09-29, diagnosed live)
- Apex Invoicing died ~30x in 24h and 4x in 30 min with ZERO crash tracebacks in server.log. Root cause was NOT the server: box at load ~12 on 2 CPUs starved the keepalive's own 15s curl probe, the probe timed out (HTTP 000), and the keepalive murdered a HEALTHY server — then restarted it into the same storm. "The keepalive becomes the outage."
- Same day, the workshop keepalive's 3s probe failed during the storm, restarted, and triggered the documented port-walk-up race (two writers, config drift) — the false kill was the first domino.
- Fix applied to both keepalives (reversible, $0): (1) probe timeout raised (apex 15s→30s, workshop 3s→15s); (2) load gate — if 1-min load > 8, never restart on a probe timeout, log and let the next poll retry; (3) workshop: if :$PORT is listening but the HTTP probe failed, skip the restart (no duplicate writers).
- General rule: before "restarting" anything, distinguish a dead process from a starved probe — check `ss -ltn` for the listener and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` for the process. A probe timeout under high load is evidence about the LOAD, not about the service.
- Load-gate refinement (2026-09-29): the load gate can now misclassify a REAL death as a starved probe — apex server was provably dead (stale PID 4177, no 18811 listener, curl exit 7 refused) while the keepalive declined restart "under load storm". Proposed hardening (not applied): when the load gate fires, still restart if the process is provably dead — no /proc/<pid> AND no listener AND curl exit 7 (refused). A curl timeout (exit 28) stays a skip. Matches the workshop-keepalive block the same afternoon (port 18805 dark, no restart, load 13.66).
detail: section: Keepalive false-kill pattern: load storm vs dead service (2026-09-29, diagnosed live)

## Bulk I/O discipline on the 2-core VM (2026-09-27, WO-CLAUDE-008)
- **Never recursive-grep `~/workspace`.** Use `rg` with an excludes file (models/, kaggle-kernels/,
  backups/, node_modules/, vendor/). A 16-min recursive grep over 62GB at load 11+ is how the box
  ends up unusable.
- **Bulk I/O runs under `nice -n 19 ionice -c3`** (backups, scans, uploads). No exceptions.
- **No builder dispatch while 1-min load > 6.** Check first, queue instead.
- **My own dispatch pattern:** never pipe a builder run through `| tail -30` again — full stdout goes
  to `state/runs/<WO>.log`, and I tail the file. (The audit caught me throwing away the evidence.)
- A background `for i in seq; do poll; sleep 600; done` loop WILL be SIGKILLed when the runtime GCs the finished tool call's cgroup (same root cause as the proxy deaths — verified 2026-09-23: the phoenix v7 monitor died after poll 1, leaving a stale "RUNNING" log line for 2h while the kernel was actually ERROR).
- Pattern for watching anything long-lived: a cron that does ONE poll per run and exits. Terminal state (COMPLETE/ERROR) is recorded in the log + state file and the loop stops itself. Never trust a monitor log line older than the cron interval — verify against the live source.
- **pkill -f footgun:** the pattern matches your own shell's cmdline. Use the bracket trick: `pkill -f "[d]ockerd"`.
- **The bracket trick must cover EVERY literal in the pattern, and kill/start go in separate calls (2026-10-04, self-inflicted x2).** `pkill -f 'a2a_gateway'` killed my own shell twice in one session — the pattern text sits in the shell's own arguments. And `pkill -f 'x[.]py'` in a line that ALSO contains `nohup python3 .../x.py --daemon` still self-matches, because the restart half carries the unbracketed literal. Rule: bracket every literal (`[a]2a_gateway`), and never put the kill and the restart in the same command line.
- **pkill --echo is NOT a dry run (2026-09-29, self-inflicted):** `--echo` prints the matched command but pkill still delivers the signal — a "verify with pkill --echo" one-liner killed the healthy reel-studio serve process. For identity checks, read /proc/<pid>/cmdline; never pkill to inspect.
detail: section: Bulk I/O discipline on the 2-core VM (2026-09-27, WO-CLAUDE-008)

text: - **NEVER `pkill -f ""` (2026-09-27, self-inflicted outage).** An empty pattern matches EVERYTHING the user can signal — it SIGTERMs the whole box (apex server, every model proxy, your own shell). Zane did this during the apex-invoicing keepalive and took down the fleet; the 5-min keepalives rebuilt most of it within ~2 min, and the rest (gemini, openrouter) were manually kicked via their own keepalive scripts. There is no legitimate use of a blanket pkill. Kill by verified PID (check /proc/<pid>/cmdline first) or not at all.

## Downloads through the egress proxy: verify, don't trust (2026-09-26, hard-won)
- urllib through the proxy can return a TRUNCATED read as clean EOF — `r.read()` returns b"" early with no IncompleteRead raised, so the skill's 3x retry loop never fires and you get a silently corrupt file (observed: Kaggle kernel harvest with vectors.npy/idf.npy/manifest.json all truncated at random points, twice).
- Rule: every downloaded artifact gets a validity check (np.load shape, json parse, checksum) before use. curl is the safer downloader here — it exits 18 on partial transfer. When a file fails validation, re-fetch with curl and re-validate until clean.
- Kaggle harvests (2026-09-26, verified): `kaggle.py output` (ListKernelSessionOutput + urllib on signed URLs) truncates silently through the proxy — adapter 4.9MB short, tokenizer 5.5MB short, run_report cut mid-string, zero exceptions raised. Re-fetch each broken file with curl against a FRESH signed URL (fetch URL + curl in one call; old ones 404 within minutes). Status polling: kernels/list returns stub entries with status=? — ground truth is the ListKernelSessionOutput RPC file list + log tail (nbconvert __results__.html write = end-of-run marker). GetKernelSessionStatus/GetKernel RPCs 403 on this token (kernels.get denied).
detail: section: Downloads through the egress proxy: verify, don't trust (2026-09-26, hard-won)

## Keepalive probe timeouts: the 10s functional probe was the killer (2026-09-26, diagnosed live)
- At ~03:11-03:21Z a flap killed most proxies; keepalives restarted them, then
  IMMEDIATELY kept killing the healthy replacements: the functional probe used
  `curl --max-time 10`, but cold-start upstream egress latency was 25-45s
  (measured: groq /v1/models 200 in 24.9s, zai 40.7s). "Listening but failing
  functional probe" -> kill -> restart -> still slow -> kill... a 5-minute
  death loop across groq, zai, nvidia, gemini.
- Fix applied to all six *_proxy_keepalive.sh: (1) cold-start grace — skip the
  functional probe entirely when the pidfile process is <180s old; (2) probe
  timeout raised 10s -> 90s (anthropic 20s -> 90s). A slow 200 is a PASS; only
  502/000/hang means the proxy itself is broken. Verified: groq keepalive now
  exits 0 without touching a 50s-old healthy proxy.
- Rule: a functional probe's timeout must exceed the worst measured cold-start
  latency with margin, or the keepalive becomes the outage.
detail: section: Keepalive probe timeouts: the 10s functional probe was the killer (2026-09-26, diagnosed live)

## Egress MITM CA rotates — long-lived TLS processes go stale (2026-09-26, hard-won)
- The egress proxy's MITM CA ROTATES (bundle `/run/hatch/egress-tls/ca-bundle.pem` replaced, observed 08:46 UTC). A Python process started before a rotation keeps its old CA in the SSL context: the socket stays listening but every upstream call 502s with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED.
- A keepalive that only checks "is the port listening" will NEVER self-heal this — the process looks alive. Keepalives for TLS proxies must do a FUNCTIONAL probe (e.g. GET /v1/models expecting 200) and restart on failure.
- Applied 2026-09-26: openrouter_proxy_keepalive.sh now probes `http://127.0.0.1:18790/v1/models` for HTTP 200; on mismatch it pkill-restarts the proxy. Same pattern applied the same morning to gemini, nvidia, and anthropic keepalives after all three went stale (18789/18791: GET /v1/models must be 200; 18792: POST /v1/messages must return a well-formed upstream error like 400, not 502). Anthropic is UP but UNFUNDED (400 "credit balance is too low") — that's the account's standing state, not a proxy bug.
- RULE: any long-lived TLS client behind the egress proxy gets a functional-probe keepalive, never a port check alone.
detail: section: Egress MITM CA rotates — long-lived TLS processes go stale (2026-09-26, hard-won)

- This broke prisma-python's engine health-check HTTP (every connect attempt) with a misleading traceback far from the real cause.

- Same session also: pg_tunnel died ~06:32 UTC from an unexplained cause (last log: egress-proxy CONNECT refused); keepalive restarts it if 5433 goes quiet, which self-healed on next run. If tunnel deaths recur, investigate the egress proxy flapping.

## Bridge mailbox push mechanics (2026-09-30, self-inflicted)
- `mailbox.py push` scans ONLY top-level `bridge/outbox/*.json`. Files in per-recipient subdirs (`outbox/claude/`, `outbox/astra/`) are NEVER pushed — they sit there silently looking sent. Stage envelopes directly at top level.
- `envelope_sha256` must be computed over `bridge.canonical_envelope(env)` = `json.dumps(env, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)`. Default `json.dumps` separators/spacing produce a different hash and the HASH_GUARD refuses the push. Don't hand-roll it.
- Evidence this bit us: the WO-AURUM-007 decisions "relayed to Claude" at 05:17Z sat unpushed in `outbox/claude/` for ~40 min until discovered; the far end never saw it.
- **Wrong staged shape = nested envelope_sha256 (2026-10-02).** A hand-staged outbox file `{"envelope": {..., "envelope_sha256": ...}}` (hash nested inside the envelope, no top-level record fields) makes `mailbox.py push` fail HASH_GUARD with `envelope_sha256 None != recomputed <hash>`. Fix: rebuild the record as `{"envelope": env, "envelope_sha256": sha256(canonical_envelope(env)), "status": "PENDING_TRANSPORT", "transport": None, "staged_at": now}` with the `envelope_sha256` key REMOVED from inside the envelope. The hash value itself survives unchanged (content was never corrupt). After fixing, verify no other staged files share the defect before re-running push, then confirm the repo copy's hash matches.
detail: section: Bridge mailbox push mechanics (2026-09-30, self-inflicted)

## hatch_gws_cli Gmail CLI needs IPv6 egress proxy (2026-10-07)
- `hatch_gws_cli gmail` API calls fail with "error sending request for url" (or stall) on the default proxy env: the Go binary resolves `hatch-egress-proxy` to the IPv4 blackhole `198.19.0.1` (which is also in no_proxy, so it bypasses the proxy and dies direct). curl works; the CLI does not.
- Fix: point proxy vars at the IPv6 address directly: `PY='http://hatch-runtime:<cred>@[fd8b:4f84:7d32:99::1]:3128'` then export HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (upper+lower). Same class of failure as Java's (see Java section).
- Wrapper: `~/workspace/goals/apex-forge-empire-build/hidden_files/gws.sh` (0700 — the proxy URL embeds the egress credential).
- Note: CLI's first probe `hatch_gws_cli gmail accounts` works offline (no network), so a working `accounts` + failing API calls = proxy/DNS issue, not a Gmail disconnect.
- **Consumers of the CLI must go through the wrapper, not the bare binary (2026-10-08).** maya's `genesis-os/maya/sweep.py` called `hatch_gws_cli` directly and every sweep hung/timed out; fixed to exec the gws wrapper path by default (overridable via `HATCH_GWS_CLI` env). Any other cron/script that shells out to `hatch_gws_cli` (apex-reply-ingest et al.) needs the same treatment or it dies on the IPv4 blackhole.
- **The egress proxy credential ROTATES — gws.sh embeds a stale one (2026-10-09, bitten live).** The wrapper's hardcoded password stopped matching the live `$https_proxy` credential (sha mismatch), so API calls failed with "error sending request" until a fresh URL was built from the live env (`urlsplit(os.environ['https_proxy']).password` + IPv6 host). If the wrapper suddenly dies again, diff its credential hash against the live env before chasing anything else. Durable fix (not yet applied): wrapper should rebuild the URL from the live env at each invocation instead of embedding a credential.
- **HTTPS CONNECT through the IPv6 proxy can be extremely slow (~15–25s/request, 2026-10-09).** TCP connects instantly and plain-HTTP is fast; only CONNECT tunnels crawl. The Go CLI's internal timeout fires before the tunnel completes → treat "error sending request" on a healthy connection as "slow egress, retry with patience", not a broken CLI. Give long yields; the proxy warms up after the first successful tunnel.
detail: section: hatch_gws_cli Gmail CLI needs IPv6 egress proxy (2026-10-07)

## PATH shims must never symlink over the name the target execs (2026-10-07, self-inflicted)
- gws.sh ends with `exec hatch_gws_cli "$@"`. I made /tmp/gwsbin/hatch_gws_cli a SYMLINK to gws.sh, then `cat >` into it — the write followed the link and destroyed the real gws.sh (0700, held a credential). Two compounding failures: (1) symlink-over-exec-name write = clobber; (2) even as a symlink it caused infinite exec-recursion (gws.sh's `exec hatch_gws_cli` re-resolved to the shim via PATH).
- Rule: a PATH shim for a wrapper must be a REAL script that strips itself from PATH (PATH=${PATH//\/tmp\/shimdir:/}) before exec'ing the wrapper by absolute path — no symlinks, no credential copies.
- Repaired: restored gws.sh byte-identical (0700) and verified live. Incident + needed durable fix for the apex-reply-ingest cron (bare `hatch_gws_cli` dies on the IPv4 blackhole; needs the wrapper's IPv6 proxy env) logged in ~/memory/2026-10-07.md.

- **False-down probes when stdin is an open pipe (2026-10-09, root-caused live).** The keepalive probe reported penguin DOWN for 77 straight runs while penguin was UP the whole time. Cause: the probe ran chromebook-ssh without stdin redirect; the wrapper's stdin-buffering read (added 2026-10-08) blocks forever on an open non-EOF stdin (cron/worker context), so each probe burned its 180s timeout then recorded down. Fix: every chromebook-ssh call inside a script MUST carry `< /dev/null` — the TOOLS.md "from agents" guidance applies equally to cron scripts, and any script without it reports false "down" instead of failing loudly. Audit every cron/script that shells out to chromebook-ssh.
- **fleet-sweeper-probe.sh audit (2026-10-09):** both SSH probes were missing `< /dev/null` — patched both. ALSO: the phone's `df` is toybox and rejects `-B1` (`df: Unknown option 'B1'`), so the phone probe silently failed forever (phone falsely "unreachable" since Oct 5). Phone probe now uses plain `df` (1K blocks × 1024 → bytes). Verified: phone came back reachable 62% in 6.9s. Penguin verified genuinely unreachable at audit time (45s timeout even through the hardened wake path — dozing).

- **curl loopback probes need `--noproxy '*'` (2026-10-09).** curl honors `$http_proxy`/`$https_proxy` env and routes even 127.0.0.1 through the egress proxy (which denies loopback), so a plain `curl http://127.0.0.1:PORT/...` returns HTTP:000 while the service is actually healthy. Always pass `--noproxy '*'` for localhost probes.

def parse_proxy_url(url):
    """Return (host, port, auth_header|None). Auth is returned separately and
    must never be logged or persisted."""
    p = urllib.parse.urlparse(url)
    host = p.hostname
    port = p.port or 3128
    auth = None
    if p.username:
        user = urllib.parse.unquote(p.username or "")
        pw = urllib.parse.unquote(p.password or "")
        auth = "Basic " + base64.b64encode(f"{user}:{pw}".encode()).decode()
    return host, port, auth

def read_headers(sock, deadline):
    """Read an HTTP header block byte-chunked; return (header_bytes, leftover).
    Byte-chunked recv avoids over-reading tunneled bytes. Bounded by deadline
    (absolute monotonic time) and HEADER_CAP."""
    data = b""
    while b"\r\n\r\n" not in data:
        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
        if remaining <= 0:
            raise DoorError("deadline exceeded reading headers")
        sock.settimeout(remaining)
        try:
            chunk = sock.recv(4096)
        except socket.timeout:
            raise DoorError("deadline exceeded reading headers")
        if not chunk:
            raise DoorError("connection closed during headers")
        data += chunk
        if len(data) > HEADER_CAP:
            raise DoorError("header block too large")
    head, leftover = data.split(b"\r\n\r\n", 1)
    return head + b"\r\n\r\n", leftover

class HealthTracker:
    """Sliding-window outcome log + score for one door. Thread-safe."""

    def __init__(self, window_events=50, window_s=300, neutral_score=50.0):
        self.window_events = window_events
        self.window_s = window_s
        self.neutral_score = neutral_score
        self.events = []  # [{ts, ok, latency_ms, kind}]
        self.total_ok = 0
        self.total_fail = 0
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def record(self, ok, latency_ms, kind="client", ts=None):
        ts = _now() if ts is None else ts
        with self._lock:
            self.events.append({"ts": ts, "ok": bool(ok),
                                "latency_ms": float(latency_ms), "kind": kind})
            if ok:
                self.total_ok += 1
            else:
                self.total_fail += 1
            self._prune(ts)

    def _prune(self, ts=None):
        ts = _now() if ts is None else ts
        cutoff = ts - self.window_s
        self.events = [e for e in self.events if e["ts"] >= cutoff]
        if len(self.events) > self.window_events:
            self.events = self.events[-self.window_events:]

    def score(self, ts=None):
        ts = _now() if ts is None else ts
        with self._lock:
            self._prune(ts)
            if not self.events:
                return self.neutral_score
            oks = [e for e in self.events if e["ok"]]
            rate = len(oks) / len(self.events)
            if oks:
                avg_s = sum(e["latency_ms"] for e in oks) / len(oks) / 1000.0
            else:
                avg_s = 0.0
            latency_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + avg_s / 5.0)
            return 100.0 * rate * latency_factor

    def snapshot(self):
        with self._lock:
            return {"events": list(self.events),
                    "total_ok": self.total_ok, "total_fail": self.total_fail}

    def restore(self, snap):
        with self._lock:
            self.events = list(snap.get("events", []))
            self.total_ok = int(snap.get("total_ok", 0))
            self.total_fail = int(snap.get("total_fail", 0))
            self._prune()

class CircuitBreaker:
    """CLOSED -> OPEN after `failure_threshold` consecutive failures within
    `window_s`; OPEN skips for `cooldown_s`; then HALF_OPEN allows one trial.
    Clock injectable for tests."""

    CLOSED = "closed"
    OPEN = "open"
    HALF_OPEN = "half_open"

    def __init__(self, failure_threshold=2, window_s=60, cooldown_s=30,
                 clock=None):
        self.failure_threshold = failure_threshold
        self.window_s = window_s
        self.cooldown_s = cooldown_s
        self._clock = clock or _now
        self._failures = []       # timestamps of consecutive failures
        self._opened_at = None    # ts when opened, or None
        self._trial_in_flight = False
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def state(self):
        with self._lock:
            return self._state_locked()

    def _state_locked(self):
        if self._opened_at is None:
            return self.CLOSED
        if self._clock() - self._opened_at >= self.cooldown_s:
            return self.HALF_OPEN
        return self.OPEN

    def allow(self):
        """May a connection be attempted now? Claims the half-open trial."""
        with self._lock:
            st = self._state_locked()
            if st == self.CLOSED:
                return True
            if st == self.OPEN:
                return False
            # HALF_OPEN: exactly one trial
            if self._trial_in_flight:
                return False
            self._trial_in_flight = True
            return True

    def record_success(self):
        with self._lock:
            self._failures = []
            self._opened_at = None
            self._trial_in_flight = False

    def record_failure(self):
        with self._lock:
            now = self._clock()
            self._trial_in_flight = False
            if self._opened_at is not None and \
                    now - self._opened_at >= self.cooldown_s:
                # failed half-open trial -> reopen for a fresh cooldown
                self._opened_at = now
                self._failures = []
                return
            cutoff = now - self.window_s
            self._failures = [t for t in self._failures if t >= cutoff]
            self._failures.append(now)
            if len(self._failures) >= self.failure_threshold:
                self._opened_at = now
                self._failures = []

    def snapshot(self):
        with self._lock:
            return {"failures": list(self._failures),
                    "opened_at": self._opened_at}

    def restore(self, snap):
        with self._lock:
            self._failures = list(snap.get("failures", []))
            self._opened_at = snap.get("opened_at")
            self._trial_in_flight = False

class Upstream:
    def __init__(self, cfg, scoring_cfg, breaker_cfg):
        self.name = cfg["name"]
        self.enabled = bool(cfg.get("enabled", False))
        self.priority = int(cfg.get("priority", 100))
        self.note = cfg.get("note", "")
        if cfg.get("from_env"):
            raw = os.environ.get(cfg["from_env"], "")
            if not raw:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"upstream {self.name}: env {cfg['from_env']} is unset")
            self.host, self.port, self._auth = parse_proxy_url(raw)
        else:
            self.host, self.port, self._auth = parse_proxy_url(cfg["url"])
        self.tracker = HealthTracker(
            window_events=int(scoring_cfg.get("window_events", 50)),
            window_s=float(scoring_cfg.get("window_s", 300)),
            neutral_score=float(scoring_cfg.get("neutral_score", 50)))
        self.breaker = CircuitBreaker(
            failure_threshold=int(breaker_cfg.get("failure_threshold", 2)),
            window_s=float(breaker_cfg.get("window_s", 60)),
            cooldown_s=float(breaker_cfg.get("cooldown_s", 30)))

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Upstream {self.name} {self.host}:{self.port} enabled={self.enabled}>"

    def _tcp_to_door(self, deadline):
        """TCP-connect to the door itself, trying every resolved address
        (pg_tunnel discipline: the IPv4 for this proxy host is a blackhole)."""
        last_err = None
        infos = socket.getaddrinfo(self.host, self.port,
                                   type=socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        for fam, _st, _proto, _canon, sa in infos:
            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
            if remaining <= 0:
                break
            s = socket.socket(fam, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            s.settimeout(remaining)
            try:
                s.connect(sa)
                return s
            except OSError as e:
                last_err = e
                s.close()
        raise DoorError(f"door {self.name}: TCP connect failed: {last_err}")

    def open_tunnel(self, target_host, target_port, deadline):
        """CONNECT through this door; return a blocking socket for the tunnel.
        `deadline` is an absolute monotonic timestamp bounding the whole
        handshake (TCP + CONNECT response)."""
        s = self._tcp_to_door(deadline)
        try:
            lines = [f"CONNECT {target_host}:{target_port} HTTP/1.1",
                     f"Host: {target_host}:{target_port}"]
            if self._auth:
                lines.append(f"Proxy-Authorization: {self._auth}")
            s.sendall(("\r\n".join(lines) + "\r\n\r\n").encode())
            head, _leftover = read_headers(s, deadline)
            status = head.split(b"\r\n", 1)[0].decode(errors="replace")
            parts = status.split(" ", 2)
            if len(parts) < 2 or parts[1] != "200":
                raise DoorError(f"door {self.name}: CONNECT refused: {status}")
            s.settimeout(None)
            return s
        except Exception:
            s.close()
            raise

    def open_plain(self, deadline):
        """TCP connection to the door for absolute-form forwarding."""
        s = self._tcp_to_door(deadline)
        s.settimeout(None)
        return s

class Router:
    def __init__(self, config, log_fn=None):
        self.config = config
        self.log = log_fn or (lambda rec: None)
        self.deadline_s = float(config.get("door_connect_deadline_s", 5))
        self.budget_s = float(config.get("total_budget_s", 9.5))
        scoring = config.get("scoring", {})
        breaker = config.get("breaker", {})
        self.upstreams = [Upstream(c, scoring, breaker)
                          for c in config.get("upstreams", [])]
        self.by_name = {u.name: u for u in self.upstreams}
        self.lanes = config.get("lanes", [])
        self._state_lock = threading.Lock()
        self.on_change = None  # callback after any recorded outcome

    # -- lanes -------------------------------------------------------------
    def lane_for(self, target_host):
        for lane in self.lanes:
            for pat in lane.get("host_patterns", []):
                if fnmatch.fnmatch(target_host.lower(), pat.lower()):
                    return lane
        return {"name": "default", "door_order": [u.name for u in self.upstreams]}

    # -- selection ---------------------------------------------------------
    def candidates(self, lane):
        """Ordered doors to try for this lane: lane order first (unknown
        names ignored), then any remaining doors; filtered to enabled,
        breaker-available doors; within the lane order, healthier doors
        first (score desc, priority asc). HALF_OPEN doors rank last."""
        order = [n for n in lane.get("door_order", []) if n in self.by_name]
        for u in self.upstreams:
            if u.name not in order:
                order.append(u.name)
        avail = []
        for name in order:
            u = self.by_name[name]
            if not u.enabled:
                continue
            st = u.breaker.state()
            if st == CircuitBreaker.OPEN:
                continue
            avail.append((st == CircuitBreaker.HALF_OPEN, u))
        avail.sort(key=lambda t: (t[0], -t[1].tracker.score(),
                                  t[1].priority))
        return [u for _half, u in avail]

    # -- outcome accounting --------------------------------------------------
    def _record(self, upstream, ok, latency_ms, kind, target, lane_name, err=None):
        upstream.tracker.record(ok, latency_ms, kind)
        if ok:
            upstream.breaker.record_success()
        else:
            upstream.breaker.record_failure()
        rec = {"ts": _now(),
               "event": ("probe_ok" if ok else "probe_fail") if kind == "probe"
                        else ("client_ok" if ok else "client_fail"),
               "lane": lane_name, "door": upstream.name, "target": target,
               "outcome": "ok" if ok else "fail",
               "latency_ms": round(latency_ms, 1)}
        if err:
            rec["error"] = str(err)[:200]
        if upstream.breaker.state() == CircuitBreaker.OPEN and not ok:
            rec["breaker"] = "open"
        self.log(rec)
        if self.on_change:
            self.on_change()

    # -- connect with failover ----------------------------------------------
    def connect(self, target_host, target_port, lane=None):

        Raises DoorError after all candidates or the total budget."""
        lane = lane or self.lane_for(target_host)

        if not cands:
            self.log({"ts": _now(), "event": "no_door", "lane": lane["name"],
                      "door": None, "target": f"{target_host}:{target_port}",
                      "outcome": "fail", "latency_ms": 0})
            raise DoorError("no door available (all disabled or breakers open)")
        budget_end = time.monotonic() + self.budget_s
        tried = []

        self.view_path = os.path.join(self.state_dir, "router_state.json")
        self.log_path = os.path.join(self.state_dir, "router.log")
        self._log_lock = threading.Lock()

        self._last_save = 0.0

def daemonize(state_dir):
    if os.fork() > 0:
        sys.exit(0)
    os.setsid()
    if os.fork() > 0:
        sys.exit(0)
    sys.stdin.close()
    try:
        cgdir = "/sys/fs/cgroup/hatch-daemons"
        os.makedirs(cgdir, exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(cgdir, "cgroup.procs"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write(str(os.getpid()))
        print("egress-router: cgroup migration OK (pid %d)" % os.getpid(),
              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    except OSError as e:
        print("egress-router: cgroup migration FAILED: %r" % (e,),
              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    # stdout/stderr go to a SEPARATE daemon log: Service._log already appends
    # structured records to router.log, and pointing stderr at the same file
    # would double every line.
    logf = open(os.path.join(state_dir, "router.daemon.log"), "a", buffering=1)
    sys.stdout = logf
    sys.stderr = logf
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(state_dir, "router.pid"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write(str(os.getpid()))
    except OSError:
        pass

class TestCircuitBreaker(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.t = [1000.0]
        self.cb = CircuitBreaker(failure_threshold=2, window_s=60,
                                 cooldown_s=30, clock=lambda: self.t[0])

    def test_opens_at_threshold(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.cb.allow())
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.assertEqual(self.cb.state(), CircuitBreaker.CLOSED)
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.assertEqual(self.cb.state(), CircuitBreaker.OPEN)
        self.assertFalse(self.cb.allow())

    def test_success_resets_consecutive_failures(self):
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.cb.record_success()
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.assertEqual(self.cb.state(), CircuitBreaker.CLOSED)

    def test_half_open_single_trial_then_close(self):
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.t[0] += 31
        self.assertEqual(self.cb.state(), CircuitBreaker.HALF_OPEN)
        self.assertTrue(self.cb.allow())    # the one trial
        self.assertFalse(self.cb.allow())   # no second concurrent trial
        self.cb.record_success()
        self.assertEqual(self.cb.state(), CircuitBreaker.CLOSED)
        self.assertTrue(self.cb.allow())

    def test_half_open_failure_reopens(self):
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.t[0] += 31
        self.assertTrue(self.cb.allow())
        self.cb.record_failure()
        self.assertEqual(self.cb.state(), CircuitBreaker.OPEN)
        self.assertFalse(self.cb.allow())
        self.t[0] += 31
        self.assertEqual(self.cb.state(), CircuitBreaker.HALF_OPEN)

class TestFailoverIntegration(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.blackhole = BlackholeServer()
        cls.blackhole.start()
        cls.echo = EchoProxyServer()
        cls.echo.start()

    def test_stalled_door_fails_over_within_budget(self):
        r = make_router(
            [door("stall", f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.blackhole.port}", 1),
             door("good", f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.echo.port}", 2)],
            deadline=1.0, budget=2.5)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        sock, used = r.connect("example.com", 443)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
        self.assertEqual(used.name, "good")
        self.assertGreaterEqual(elapsed, 1.0)   # the stall really burned time
        self.assertLess(elapsed, 2.5)           # ...but inside the budget
        sock.sendall(b"ping-through")
        self.assertEqual(sock.recv(100), b"ping-through")
        sock.close()
        events = [rec.get("event") for rec in r.test_logs]
        self.assertIn("failover", events)
        self.assertIn("client_fail", events)

    def test_breaker_opens_and_door_is_skipped(self):
        r = make_router(
            [door("stall", f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.blackhole.port}", 1)],
            deadline=0.5, budget=1.0)
        for _ in range(2):
            with self.assertRaises(DoorError):
                r.connect("example.com", 443)
        self.assertEqual(r.by_name["stall"].breaker.state(),
                         CircuitBreaker.OPEN)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        with self.assertRaises(DoorError):
            r.connect("example.com", 443)
        # open breaker -> honest error immediately, no 0.5 s stall burn
        self.assertLess(time.monotonic() - t0, 0.4)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

class GenesisPay:
    """One Genesis Pay S0 instance over one dedicated SQLite file."""

    def __init__(self, db_path, webhook_secret=None):
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.webhook_secret = webhook_secret
        if db_path != ":memory:":
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(db_path)), exist_ok=True)
        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30)
        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self._conn.isolation_level = None  # explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE control
        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        if db_path != ":memory:":
            # Durability (Argon RALPH-004 acceptance bar): WAL + FULL sync —
            # a committed posting survives a power loss / VM recycle.
            self._conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
            self._conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = FULL")
        self._conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
        self._migrate_zero_sum(self._conn)
        for code, name, typ, side in SEED_ACCOUNTS:
            self._conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO accounts (code,name,type,normal_side,created_at) "
                "VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)", (code, name, typ, side, _iso(_now())))

    # DB-level zero-sum enforcement (Argon RALPH-004 convergence): the
    # entry declares its totals + line count up front; a trigger verifies
    # the ACTUAL line sums against the declaration the moment the final
    # line lands — so even writes that bypass the posting API cannot land
    # an unbalanced entry. The API check in _post_journal_tx remains the
    # first line of defense; this trigger is the database's own.
    _ZERO_SUM_TRIGGER = """
    CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_lines_zero_sum
    AFTER INSERT ON journal_lines
    WHEN (SELECT line_count FROM journal_entries WHERE id = NEW.entry_id) IS NOT NULL
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM journal_lines WHERE entry_id = NEW.entry_id)
          >= (SELECT line_count FROM journal_entries WHERE id = NEW.entry_id)
    BEGIN
      SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'zero-sum violation: journal entry does not balance')
      WHERE (SELECT debit_total_cents FROM journal_entries WHERE id = NEW.entry_id)
            != (SELECT credit_total_cents FROM journal_entries WHERE id = NEW.entry_id)
         OR (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) FROM journal_lines
             WHERE entry_id = NEW.entry_id AND side = 'debit')
            != (SELECT debit_total_cents FROM journal_entries WHERE id = NEW.entry_id)
         OR (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) FROM journal_lines
             WHERE entry_id = NEW.entry_id AND side = 'credit')
            != (SELECT credit_total_cents FROM journal_entries WHERE id = NEW.entry_id);
    END;
    """

    @staticmethod
    def _migrate_zero_sum(conn):
        cols = {r[1] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(journal_entries)")}
        for col in ("debit_total_cents", "credit_total_cents", "line_count"):
            if col not in cols:
                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE journal_entries ADD COLUMN %s INTEGER" % col)
        conn.executescript(GenesisPay._ZERO_SUM_TRIGGER)

    def close(self):
        self._conn.close()

    @contextmanager
    def _tx(self):
        conn = self._conn
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            yield conn
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise

    # ------------------------------------------------------- internal utils
    def _audit(self, conn, event_type, payload):
        row = conn.execute("SELECT hash FROM audit_log ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1").fetchone()
        prev = row["hash"] if row else "GENESIS_PAY_GENESIS"
        ts = _iso(_now())
        body = {"prev": prev, "type": event_type, "payload": payload, "at": ts}
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO audit_log (created_at,event_type,payload_json,prev_hash,hash) "
            "VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
            (ts, event_type, _canonical(payload), prev, _hash(body)))

    def _outbox(self, conn, topic, payload):
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO outbox_events (topic,payload_json,created_at) VALUES (?,?,?)",
                     (topic, _canonical(payload), _iso(_now())))

    def _idempotent_check(self, conn, key, payload):
        """Return stored result dict on exact replay; raise 409 on conflict."""
        if not key or not str(key).strip():
            raise ValidationError("a client idempotency key is required on every money call")
        row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM idempotency_keys WHERE key=?", (str(key),)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        if row["payload_hash"] != _hash(payload):
            raise ConflictError(
                "idempotency key %r was already used with a different payload" % key)
        return json.loads(row["result_json"])

    def _idempotent_store(self, conn, key, payload, result):

    def _ensure_account(self, conn, code):

            ACCT_AR: ("Accounts receivable", "asset", "debit"),

        if code.startswith(ACCT_CLEARING_PREFIX):

                     "VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)", (code, name, typ, side, _iso(_now())))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- ledger
    def post_journal(self, lines, memo, currency, external_ref=None,
                     reversal_of=None, idempotency_key=None):
        """Post one balanced double-entry journal entry.

        lines: [{"account": code, "side": "debit"|"credit", "amount_cents": int}]
        Key + journal (+ external-ref map, audit, outbox) commit atomically.
        """
        currency = _check_currency(currency)
        payload = {"lines": lines, "memo": memo, "currency": currency,
                   "external_ref": external_ref, "reversal_of": reversal_of}
        with self._tx() as conn:
            if idempotency_key:
                stored = self._idempotent_check(conn, idempotency_key, payload)
                if stored is not None:
                    return stored
            entry = self._post_journal_tx(conn, lines, memo, currency,
                                          external_ref, reversal_of)
            result = {"entry_id": entry, "external_ref": external_ref,
                      "external_ref_flag": "mapped" if external_ref else "unmapped_flagged",
                      "currency": currency}
            if idempotency_key:
                self._idempotent_store(conn, idempotency_key, payload, result)
            self._audit(conn, "journal.posted", result)
            self._outbox(conn, "journal.posted", result)
            return result

    def _post_journal_tx(self, conn, lines, memo, currency, external_ref, reversal_of=None):
        if not isinstance(lines, list) or len(lines) < 2:
            raise ValidationError("a journal entry needs at least two lines")
        debits = credits = 0
        norm = []
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
            amount = _check_money(ln.get("amount_cents"), "lines[%d].amount_cents" % i)
            side = ln.get("side")
            if side not in ("debit", "credit"):
                raise ValidationError("lines[%d].side must be debit|credit" % i)
            if _check_currency(ln.get("currency", currency)) != currency:
                raise ValidationError("all lines of an entry share one explicit currency")
            self._ensure_account(conn, ln["account"])
            norm.append((ln["account"], side, amount))
            if side == "debit":
                debits += amount
            else:
                credits += amount

    def create_tap_request(self, kind, payload, initiator, expires_in_seconds=3600,
                           destination=None):
        """C8: creating a movement/refund/payout ONLY creates an immutable
        Brandon tap request bound to the payload hash. Nothing executes."""
        if kind not in ("refund", "payout", "movement"):
            raise ValidationError("tap request kind must be refund|payout|movement")
        if not initiator or not str(initiator).strip():
            raise ValidationError("initiator is required (four-eyes needs a named initiator)")
        if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not payload:
            raise ValidationError("tap request payload must be a non-empty dict")
        now = _now()
        req_id = _new_id("tap")
        record = {"id": req_id, "kind": kind, "payload": payload,
                  "payload_hash": _hash(payload), "destination": destination,
                  "amount_cents": payload.get("amount_cents"),
                  "currency": payload.get("currency"), "initiator": str(initiator),
                  "status": "pending", "created_at": _iso(now),
                  "expires_at": _iso(now + timedelta(seconds=int(expires_in_seconds)))}
        with self._tx() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO tap_requests (id,kind,payload_json,payload_hash,destination,"
                "amount_cents,currency,initiator,status,created_at,expires_at) "
                "VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?, 'pending', ?, ?)",
                (req_id, kind, _canonical(payload), record["payload_hash"], destination,
                 record["amount_cents"], record["currency"], str(initiator),
                 record["created_at"], record["expires_at"]))
            self._audit(conn, "tap.requested", record)
            self._outbox(conn, "tap.requested", record)
        return record

    def get_tap_request(self, request_id):
        row = self._conn.execute("SELECT * FROM tap_requests WHERE id=?",
                                 (request_id,)).fetchone()

            raise NotFoundError("tap request %s not found" % request_id)
        d = dict(row)

            if not row:

            req = dict(row)
            if actor != "brandon":
                raise GateError("only actor 'brandon' may approve a money movement")
            if req["initiator"] == actor:
                raise GateError("four-eyes: initiator may not approve their own request")

            if _parse_iso(req["expires_at"]) <= now:
                conn.execute("UPDATE tap_requests SET status='expired' WHERE id=?",
                             (request_id,))
                raise GateError("tap request has expired; a fresh request is required")

                raise GateError("tap request is %s, not pending" % row["status"])
            conn.execute("UPDATE tap_requests SET status='rejected', approver=? WHERE id=?",
                         (actor, request_id))
            self._audit(conn, "tap.rejected", {"request_id": request_id})
            return {"request_id": request_id, "status": "rejected"}

    def prepare_instruction(self, request_id, now=None):
        """An approved request yields a PREPARED INSTRUCTION ONLY.

        There is intentionally no send/execute adapter anywhere in this
        package: a human (Brandon) performs the movement on the real rail
        and the result is recorded back with its external reference.
        """
        now = now or _now()
        req = self.get_tap_request(request_id)
        if req["status"] != "approved":
            raise GateError("instruction can be prepared only from an approved "
                            "request (status=%s)" % req["status"])
        if _parse_iso(req["expires_at"]) <= now:
            raise GateError("approval has expired; a fresh request is required")
        if _hash(req["payload"]) != req["payload_hash"]:
            raise GateError("payload hash mismatch — approval no longer binds")
        return {"status": "prepared_only", "executed": False, "adapter": None,
                "request_id": request_id, "kind": req["kind"],
                "instruction": req["payload"], "payload_hash": req["payload_hash"],
                "destination": req["destination"],
                "note": "Prepared only. No adapter exists to send this; Brandon "
                        "executes on the rail and the outcome is recorded back."}

    def change_tap_destination(self, request_id, new_destination, initiator,
                               cooldown_seconds=3600, expires_in_seconds=3600):
        """Destination change invalidates the prior approval (I-20) and
        creates a fresh request carrying a cooldown timestamp."""
        old = self.get_tap_request(request_id)
        payload = dict(old["payload"])
        payload["destination"] = new_destination
        with self._tx() as conn:
            conn.execute("UPDATE tap_requests SET status='invalidated' WHERE id=?",
                         (request_id,))
            self._audit(conn, "tap.invalidated_by_destination_change",
                        {"request_id": request_id, "new_destination": new_destination})
        new_req = self.create_tap_request(old["kind"], payload, initiator,
                                          expires_in_seconds=expires_in_seconds,
                                          destination=new_destination)
        with self._tx() as conn:
            conn.execute("UPDATE tap_requests SET cooldown_until=? WHERE id=?",
                         (_iso(_now() + timedelta(seconds=int(cooldown_seconds))),
                          new_req["id"]))
        new_req["cooldown_until"] = _iso(_now() + timedelta(seconds=int(cooldown_seconds)))
        new_req["supersedes"] = request_id
        return new_req

    def refundable_cents(self, invoice_ref):
        """Ledger-level cap base (I-17): captured - refunds - dispute losses."""
        conn = self._conn
        captured = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS s FROM payment_intents "
            "WHERE invoice_ref=? AND state IN ('confirmed','settling','settled',"
            "'disputed','partially_refunded')", (str(invoice_ref),)).fetchone()["s"]
        refunded = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS s FROM refunds WHERE invoice_ref=?",
            (str(invoice_ref),)).fetchone()["s"]
        losses = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS s FROM disputes "
            "WHERE invoice_ref=? AND status='lost'", (str(invoice_ref),)).fetchone()["s"]
        return int(captured) - int(refunded) - int(losses)

        """Record a refund that Brandon approved (tap) and executed manually.

        Posts Dr Refunds / Cr Bank cash (settled) or Cr Clearing.

                   "external_ref": external_ref}

            stored = self._idempotent_check(conn, idempotency_key, payload)

            req = dict(req_row)
            if req["kind"] != "refund" or req["status"] != "approved":
                raise GateError("refunds post only against an approved refund tap "
                                "request (status=%s)" % req["status"])

    def ingest_webhook(self, provider, event_id, payload, signature=None, secret=None):

            raw = payload.encode("utf-8")

        verified = 0

            if not signature:
                raise SignatureError("webhook secret configured but no signature sent")

                                hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

                raise SignatureError("webhook HMAC verification failed (fail closed)")

                        "provider": provider, "event_id": str(event_id),
                        "verified": bool(existing["verified"])}

                "INSERT INTO webhook_inbox (provider,event_id,payload_json,verified,"
                "received_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
                (provider, str(event_id), _canonical(body), verified, _iso(_now())))
            result = {"duplicate": False, "inbox_id": cur.lastrowid,
                      "provider": provider, "event_id": str(event_id),
                      "verified": bool(verified)}
            self._audit(conn, "webhook.ingested", result)
            self._outbox(conn, "webhook.ingested", result)

class TestReconciliation(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_clean_three_way_match(self):

        out = p.reconcile(

              "fee_cents": 300, "status": "settled"}],
            [{"external_ref": "ext-pay-1", "amount_cents": 29400}])
        self.assertEqual(out["matched"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(out["breaks"], 0)

    def test_breaks_persist_as_open_exceptions(self):
        p, r = issued_pay()
        p.record_settlement(r["intent_id"], "k-settle", fee_cents=300)
        out = p.reconcile(
            [{"external_ref": "ext-pay-1", "amount_cents": 29700,
              "fee_cents": 300, "status": "settled"}],
            [{"external_ref": "ext-pay-1", "amount_cents": 29000}])  # short deposit
        self.assertEqual(out["breaks"], 1)
        exc = p.list_exceptions(status="open")
        self.assertEqual(len(exc), 1)
        self.assertEqual(exc[0]["break_type"], "amount_mismatch")
        self.assertTrue(exc[0]["owner"])
        self.assertTrue(exc[0]["sla_due"])
        # Breaks are never auto-closed: a clean re-run adds a run, the old
        # exception stays open until a human closes it off-ledger.
        p.reconcile(
            [{"external_ref": "ext-pay-1", "amount_cents": 29700,
              "fee_cents": 300, "status": "settled"}],
            [{"external_ref": "ext-pay-1", "amount_cents": 29400}])
        self.assertEqual(len(p.list_exceptions(status="open")), 1)

    def test_missing_everywhere_breaks(self):
        p, r = issued_pay()
        out = p.reconcile([], [])
        self.assertGreaterEqual(out["breaks"], 1)
        types = {e["break_type"] for e in p.list_exceptions()}
        self.assertIn("missing_in_settlement", types)

def _format_bits(mask):
    data = mask  # EC level M -> indicator bits 00, so data = 0b00<<3 | mask

def qr_svg(data, scale=6, border=4):
    """Render a QR code for *data* as a standalone SVG string."""
    _v, size, matrix, _mask = _qr_matrix(data)
    dim = (size + 2 * border) * scale
    parts = ['<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="%d" height="%d" '
             'viewBox="0 0 %d %d">' % (dim, dim, dim, dim),
             '<rect width="%d" height="%d" fill="#ffffff"/>' % (dim, dim)]
    for r in range(size):
        for c in range(size):
            if matrix[r][c]:
                parts.append('<rect x="%d" y="%d" width="%d" height="%d" '
                             'fill="#000000"/>'
                             % ((c + border) * scale, (r + border) * scale,
                                scale, scale))
    parts.append("</svg>")
    return "".join(parts)

def _extract_codewords(matrix, fn, size, mask):
    bits = []
    upward = True
    x = size - 1
    while x > 0:
        if x == 6:
            x -= 1
        rows = range(size - 1, -1, -1) if upward else range(size)
        for y in rows:
            for xx in (x, x - 1):
                if not fn[y][xx]:
                    dark = matrix[y][xx]
                    if ((mask == 0 and (y + xx) % 2 == 0) or
                        (mask == 1 and y % 2 == 0) or
                        (mask == 2 and xx % 3 == 0) or
                        (mask == 3 and (y + xx) % 3 == 0) or
                        (mask == 4 and (y // 2 + xx // 3) % 2 == 0) or
                        (mask == 5 and (y * xx) % 2 + (y * xx) % 3 == 0) or
                        (mask == 6 and ((y * xx) % 2 + (y * xx) % 3) % 2 == 0) or
                        (mask == 7 and ((y + xx) % 2 + (y * xx) % 3) % 2 == 0)):
                        dark = not dark
                    bits.append(1 if dark else 0)
        upward = not upward
        x -= 2
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(0, len(bits) - 7, 8):
        byte = 0
        for bit in bits[i:i + 8]:
            byte = (byte << 1) | bit
        out.append(byte)
    return bytes(out)

class TestQrEncoder(unittest.TestCase):
    PAYLOADS = ["https://cash.app/$zanehart369",
                "https://www.paypal.me/ApexForge/297",
                "A", "x" * 100]

    def test_matrix_structure_and_format_bits(self):
        for payload in self.PAYLOADS:
            with self.subTest(payload=payload[:24]):
                version, size, matrix, mask, _fn = _qr_matrix(
                    payload, _return_fn=True)
                self.assertEqual(size, 4 * version + 17)
                # finder pattern corners
                self.assertTrue(matrix[0][0] and matrix[0][6]
                                and matrix[6][0] and not matrix[1][1])
                self.assertTrue(matrix[size - 8][8])  # dark module
                # read format bits back (first copy) and compare
                fb = 0
                pos = {}
                for i in range(6):
                    pos[i] = matrix[i][8]
                pos[6] = matrix[7][8]
                pos[7] = matrix[8][8]
                pos[8] = matrix[8][7]
                for i in range(9, 15):
                    pos[i] = matrix[8][14 - i]
                for i in range(15):
                    if pos[i]:
                        fb |= (1 << i)
                self.assertEqual(fb, _format_bits(mask))

    def test_decode_back_round_trip_and_zero_syndromes(self):
        for payload in self.PAYLOADS:
            with self.subTest(payload=payload[:24]):
                version, size, matrix, mask, fn = _qr_matrix(
                    payload, _return_fn=True)
                stream = _extract_codewords(matrix, fn, size, mask)
                expected = _interleave(
                    _data_codewords(payload.encode(), version), version)
                self.assertEqual(stream[:len(expected)], expected)
                blocks, ecs = _deinterleave(stream, version)
                ec_len, _g = _QR_M_BLOCKS[version]
                for block, ecc in zip(blocks, ecs):
                    self.assertEqual(_rs_encode(block + ecc, ec_len),
                                     bytes(ec_len),
                                     "RS syndrome must be zero")
                data = b"".join(blocks)
                bits = "".join(format(b, "08b") for b in data)
                self.assertEqual(bits[:4], "0100")  # byte mode
                ln = int(bits[4:12], 2)
                got = bytes(int(bits[12 + 8 * i:20 + 8 * i], 2)
                            for i in range(ln))
                self.assertEqual(got.decode(), payload)

"""Genesis Vault ledger: personal-treasury records beside Genesis Pay.

Same discipline as Genesis Pay S0: integer cents only, double entry with a
zero-sum trigger, append-only postings, idempotency keys, a hash-chained audit
log, WAL + synchronous=FULL.

The Vault RECORDS money facts that Brandon enters by hand or imports from his
own statements. It never moves money, never holds credentials, never talks to a
bank or payment app. There is deliberately no network or subprocess code in
this package (a test enforces it).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
import re
import sqlite3
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
from pathlib import Path

INSTITUTIONS = ("cash_app", "paypal", "current", "onepay", "chime", "robinhood", "bank", "internal")
OUTCOMES = ("paid", "arranged", "disputed", "cancelled")
SLUG_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,39}\Z")
RECONCILIATION = "reconciliation"
GENESIS_HASH = "0" * 64

# Cents columns are declared WITHOUT a type on purpose: an INTEGER column's type
# affinity would silently turn the text '5.00' (dollars) into the integer 5 (cents)
# before any CHECK or trigger sees it. With no affinity, typeof() rejects it.
SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('asset', 'liability', 'equity')),
    institution TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (institution IN
        ('cash_app', 'paypal', 'current', 'onepay', 'chime', 'robinhood', 'bank', 'internal')),
    buffer_cents NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
        CHECK (typeof(buffer_cents) = 'integer' AND buffer_cents >= 0),
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    effective_date TEXT NOT NULL,
    memo TEXT NOT NULL,
    source TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('manual', 'statement_import', 'balance_assertion')),
    posted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (posted IN (0, 1)),
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS postings (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    entry_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES entries(id),
    account_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    amount_cents NOT NULL
        CHECK (typeof(amount_cents) = 'integer' AND amount_cents <> 0)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS obligations (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    account_id INTEGER REFERENCES accounts(id),
    payee TEXT NOT NULL,
    amount_cents NOT NULL CHECK (typeof(amount_cents) = 'integer' AND amount_cents > 0),
    due_date TEXT,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('bill', 'scheduled_debit')),
    notice TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'
        CHECK (status IN ('open', 'paid', 'arranged', 'disputed', 'cancelled')),
    outcome_note TEXT,
    outcome_at TEXT,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log (

    ts TEXT NOT NULL,
    event TEXT NOT NULL,
    payload TEXT NOT NULL,
    prev_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    hash TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- Postings are append-only and may only be added to an entry that is not yet posted.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS postings_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON postings
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'postings are append-only'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS postings_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON postings
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'postings are append-only'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS postings_only_on_open_entry BEFORE INSERT ON postings
WHEN (SELECT posted FROM entries WHERE id = NEW.entry_id) IS NOT 0
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'entry is posted or missing'); END;

-- Zero-sum: an entry can only become posted if it has 2+ postings summing to 0.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS entries_zero_sum BEFORE UPDATE ON entries
WHEN NEW.posted = 1 AND (
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM postings WHERE entry_id = NEW.id) < 2
    OR (SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM postings WHERE entry_id = NEW.id) <> 0)
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'unbalanced entry: postings must be 2+ and sum to zero'); END;
-- The only permitted update is open -> posted with nothing else changed.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS entries_immutable BEFORE UPDATE ON entries
WHEN OLD.posted = 1 OR NEW.posted <> 1 OR NEW.id <> OLD.id

    OR NEW.memo IS NOT OLD.memo OR NEW.source IS NOT OLD.source OR NEW.created_at IS NOT OLD.created_at
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'entries are immutable once posted'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS entries_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON entries
WHEN OLD.posted = 1
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'posted entries cannot be deleted'); END;

-- Obligations: the only change is Brandon recording one outcome on an open item.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS obligations_outcome_once BEFORE UPDATE ON obligations
WHEN OLD.status <> 'open' OR NEW.status = 'open'
    OR NEW.amount_cents IS NOT OLD.amount_cents OR NEW.payee IS NOT OLD.payee
    OR NEW.due_date IS NOT OLD.due_date OR NEW.account_id IS NOT OLD.account_id
    OR NEW.kind IS NOT OLD.kind OR NEW.idempotency_key IS NOT OLD.idempotency_key
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'obligation outcome can be recorded once, on an open item'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS obligations_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON obligations
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'obligations cannot be deleted; record an outcome'); END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS audit_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON audit_log
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'audit log is append-only'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS audit_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON audit_log
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'audit log is append-only'); END;

        return max(d for d in (row["d"], stated) if d) if (row["d"] or stated) else None

    def balance_known(self, slug: str) -> bool:
        aid = self._account_id(slug)
        return self.db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM postings p JOIN entries e ON e.id = p.entry_id "
                               "WHERE e.posted = 1 AND p.account_id = ? LIMIT 1", (aid,)).fetchone() is not None \
            or self.db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM audit_log WHERE event = 'balance.assert' AND json_extract(payload, '$.account') = ? LIMIT 1",
                               (slug,)).fetchone() is not None

    def ledger_total(self) -> int:
        return self.db.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(p.amount_cents), 0) AS s FROM postings p "
                               "JOIN entries e ON e.id = p.entry_id WHERE e.posted = 1").fetchone()["s"]

    def set_balance(self, slug: str, amount: str | int, as_of: str, *, key: str | None = None,
                    source: str = "balance_assertion") -> int | None:
        """Brandon states a balance he read in the app or on a statement. The difference is
        booked against the reconciliation equity account so the ledger stays zero-sum."""
        target = parse_cents(amount)
        as_of = _iso_date(as_of)
        if self.db.execute("SELECT kind FROM accounts WHERE slug = ?", (slug,)).fetchone() is None:
            raise VaultError(f"unknown account: {slug!r}")
        delta = target - self.balance(slug)
        if key is not None:
            # Caller-supplied key: a collision is a true duplicate submission.
            if self.db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM entries WHERE idempotency_key = ?", (key,)).fetchone():
                return None
        else:
            key = f"balance:{slug}:{as_of}:{target}"
            if delta != 0:
                # Restating a value already asserted today (the balance moved
                # away and came back) must still book — dropping it leaves a
                # stale balance that can mask a shortfall. Claude Phase 2
                # review HIGH finding, 2026-10-30; regression tests in
                # tests/test_balance_restatement.py. Mint a fresh key instead.
                n = 2
                while self.db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM entries WHERE idempotency_key = ?", (key,)).fetchone():
                    key = f"balance:{slug}:{as_of}:{target}#{n}"
                    n += 1
        if delta == 0:
            with self._tx():
                self._audit("balance.assert", {"account": slug, "as_of": as_of, "cents": target, "delta": 0})
            return None
        entry = self.post_entry(key, as_of, f"Balance stated: {slug} = {fmt_cents(target)}",
                                [(slug, delta), (RECONCILIATION, -delta)], source=source)
        with self._tx():
            self._audit("balance.assert", {"account": slug, "as_of": as_of, "cents": target, "delta": delta})
        return entry

    def record_completed_transfer(self, key: str, from_slug: str, to_slug: str, amount: str | int,
                                  on: str, memo: str = "") -> int:
        """Bookkeeping for a transfer Brandon ALREADY made himself in the provider's app."""
        cents = parse_cents(amount)
        if cents <= 0 or from_slug == to_slug:
            raise VaultError("transfer needs a positive amount and two different accounts")
        return self.post_entry(key, on, memo or f"Brandon moved {fmt_cents(cents)} {from_slug} -> {to_slug}",
                               [(from_slug, -cents), (to_slug, cents)], source="manual")

    def import_balances_csv(self, text: str, *, source_name: str = "statement") -> int:
        """CSV with header account,balance,as_of. All rows apply or none do."""
        file_hash = hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text)))
        if not rows or set(rows[0]) != {"account", "balance", "as_of"}:
            raise VaultError("CSV header must be exactly: account,balance,as_of")
        parsed = []
        for i, r in enumerate(rows, 2):
            try:
                parsed.append((r["account"].strip(), parse_cents(r["balance"]), _iso_date(r["as_of"].strip())))
            except (VaultError, AttributeError) as exc:
                raise VaultError(f"line {i}: {exc}") from None
            self._account_id(parsed[-1][0])
        applied = 0
        with self._tx():  # one transaction: a failing row leaves nothing behind
            for i, (slug, cents, as_of) in enumerate(parsed):
                if self.set_balance(slug, cents, as_of, key=f"import:{file_hash}:{i}", source="statement_import"):
                    applied += 1
            self._audit("import.balances", {"source": source_name, "sha256_16": file_hash, "rows": len(parsed)})
        return applied

class Ledger(Base):

        self.assertEqual(self.v.db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys").fetchone()[0], 1)

        self.assertEqual(self.state(), before)

    def test_unbalanced_entry_rejected_by_trigger_raw_sql(self):
        a = self.v.add_account("cash_app", "Cash App", "cash_app")
        db = self.v.db
        db.execute("INSERT INTO entries (idempotency_key, effective_date, memo, source, created_at) "
                   "VALUES ('raw', '2026-10-30', 'raw', 'manual', 'now')")
        eid = db.execute("SELECT id FROM entries WHERE idempotency_key='raw'").fetchone()[0]
        db.execute("INSERT INTO postings (entry_id, account_id, amount_cents) VALUES (?, ?, 100)", (eid, a))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(sqlite3.IntegrityError, "unbalanced"):
            db.execute("UPDATE entries SET posted = 1 WHERE id = ?", (eid,))
        self.assertEqual(self.v.balance("cash_app"), 0)  # unposted entries never count

    def test_single_posting_and_non_integer_rejected(self):
        self.v.add_account("cash_app", "Cash App", "cash_app")
        with self.assertRaises(VaultError):
            self.v.post_entry("k", "2026-10-30", "one leg", [("cash_app", 0)])
        with self.assertRaises(VaultError):
            self.v.post_entry("k2", "2026-10-30", "float", [("cash_app", 1.5), ("reconciliation", -1.5)])
        a = self.v._account_id("cash_app")
        self.v.db.execute("INSERT INTO entries (idempotency_key, effective_date, memo, source, created_at) "
                          "VALUES ('t', '2026-10-30', 't', 'manual', 'now')")
        with self.assertRaises(sqlite3.IntegrityError):
            self.v.db.execute("INSERT INTO postings (entry_id, account_id, amount_cents) "
                              "VALUES ((SELECT id FROM entries WHERE idempotency_key='t'), ?, '5.00')", (a,))

    def test_postings_and_posted_entries_append_only(self):
        self.v.add_account("cash_app", "Cash App", "cash_app")
        eid = self.v.set_balance("cash_app", "40.00", "2026-10-30")
        db = self.v.db
        for sql in ("UPDATE postings SET amount_cents = 1", "DELETE FROM postings",
                    "UPDATE entries SET memo = 'x'", "DELETE FROM entries",
                    "UPDATE audit_log SET event = 'x'", "DELETE FROM audit_log"):
            with self.assertRaises(sqlite3.IntegrityError, msg=sql):
                db.execute(sql)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(sqlite3.IntegrityError, "posted"):
            db.execute("INSERT INTO postings (entry_id, account_id, amount_cents) VALUES (?, 1, 5)", (eid,))
        self.assertEqual(self.v.balance("cash_app"), 4000)

        e2 = self.v.post_entry("same", "2026-10-30", "m", [("cash_app", 100), ("chime", -100)])
        self.assertEqual(e1, e2)

        self.assertEqual(levels, ["UNASSIGNED", "UNKNOWN_BALANCE"])

        self.assertEqual(self.state(), before)  # nothing written: no entry, no audit record, no transfer
        self.assertEqual((self.v.balance("cash_app"), self.v.balance("robinhood")), (10000, 0))
        self.assertTrue(all(c["status"] in (rules.PREPARED, "NO_SOURCE") for c in b["sweeps"]))
        for mod in (rules, board):

def debit_watch(snap: dict, today: date, window: int = DEBIT_WINDOW_DAYS) -> list[dict]:
    """Phase 2 Watch: dated scheduled debits due within the window (overdue
    included), in due-date order, each checked cumulatively against its target
    account's balance: debits are covered in the order they will hit until the
    balance runs out. Undated items cannot be watched and are excluded here
    (the deficit guard still flags them). Coverage is a reading of recorded
    balances, not a prediction -- a balance Brandon has not entered gives
    covered=None (unknown), never a guess."""
    by_slug = {a["slug"]: a for a in snap["accounts"]}
    dated = [o for o in snap["obligations"] if o["kind"] == "scheduled_debit" and o["due_date"]
             and date.fromisoformat(o["due_date"]) <= today + timedelta(days=window)]
    dated.sort(key=lambda o: (o["due_date"], o["id"]))
    running: dict[str, int | None] = {}
    rows = []
    for o in dated:
        slug = o["account"]
        if slug not in running:
            acct = by_slug.get(slug) if slug else None
            running[slug] = acct["balance_cents"] if acct else None
        bal = running[slug]
        covered = None if bal is None else bal >= o["amount_cents"]
        short = None if bal is None else max(0, o["amount_cents"] - bal)
        if bal is not None:
            running[slug] = bal - o["amount_cents"]
        days = (date.fromisoformat(o["due_date"]) - today).days
        rows.append({"id": o["id"], "payee": o["payee"], "amount_cents": o["amount_cents"],
                     "due_date": o["due_date"], "days_until": days,
                     "when": f"OVERDUE {-days}d" if days < 0 else ("TODAY" if days == 0 else f"in {days}d"),
                     "account": slug or "unassigned",
                     "account_name": by_slug[slug]["name"] if slug in by_slug else "unassigned",
                     "covered": covered, "shortfall_cents": short})
    return rows

def due_window(snap: dict, today: date, window: int = DEBIT_WINDOW_DAYS) -> list[dict]:
    """Every dated obligation (bills and scheduled debits) due within the window."""
    rows = [r for r in bill_calendar(snap, today)
            if r["due_date"] and date.fromisoformat(r["due_date"]) <= today + timedelta(days=window)]
    return rows

def bill_calendar(snap: dict, today: date) -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for o in snap["obligations"]:
        if o["due_date"] is None:
            when, rank, days = "DATE UNKNOWN", 1, None
        else:
            days = (date.fromisoformat(o["due_date"]) - today).days
            when = f"OVERDUE {-days}d" if days < 0 else ("TODAY" if days == 0 else f"in {days}d")
            rank = 0 if days < 0 else 2
        rows.append({"id": o["id"], "payee": o["payee"], "amount_cents": o["amount_cents"], "kind": o["kind"],
                     "due_date": o["due_date"], "when": when, "account": o["account"] or "unassigned",
                     "final_notice": "final" in o["notice"].lower(), "notice": o["notice"],
                     "_sort": (rank, days if days is not None else 0, o["id"])})
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (not r["final_notice"], r["_sort"]))
    for r in rows:
        del r["_sort"]
    return rows

def sweep_suggestions(snap: dict, today: date, horizon: int = HORIZON_DAYS) -> list[dict]:
    """Ranked PREPARED_ONLY 'Move $X from A to B' cards for deficits, drawn from
    accounts with a known surplus. Ranking: earliest due date first, then the
    largest shortfall. Every card shows its math; a card sourced from Cash App
    carries the instant-fee warning (the fee is read in-app, never guessed).
    Cards are computed only -- nothing is stored and nothing is executed."""
    deficits = [f for f in deficit_guard(snap, today, horizon) if f["level"] == "DEFICIT"]
    by_slug = {a["slug"]: a for a in snap["accounts"]}

    def due_by(slug: str) -> str | None:
        dated = [o["due_date"] for o in snap["obligations"]
                 if o["account"] == slug and o["due_date"] and _due(o, today, horizon)]
        return min(dated) if dated else None

    deficits.sort(key=lambda f: (due_by(f["account"]) or "9999-99-99", -f["shortfall_cents"], f["account"]))
    surplus = {}
    deficit_slugs = {f["account"] for f in deficits}
    for a in snap["accounts"]:
        if a["kind"] != "asset" or a["balance_cents"] is None or a["slug"] in deficit_slugs:
            continue
        own_due = sum(o["amount_cents"] for o in snap["obligations"]
                      if o["account"] == a["slug"] and _due(o, today, horizon))
        free = a["balance_cents"] - own_due - a["buffer_cents"]
        if free > 0:
            surplus[a["slug"]] = {"free": free, "balance_cents": a["balance_cents"],
                                  "own_due_cents": own_due, "buffer_cents": a["buffer_cents"]}
    cards = []
    for f in deficits:
        dest = by_slug[f["account"]]
        by = due_by(f["account"])
        reason = (f"{dest['name']} has {fmt_cents(f['due_cents'])} scheduled by {by or 'an unknown date'} "
                  f"against a {fmt_cents(f['balance_cents'])} balance")
        need = f["shortfall_cents"]
        for src in sorted(surplus, key=lambda s: (-surplus[s]["free"], s)):
            if need == 0:
                break
            amt = min(need, surplus[src]["free"])
            if amt <= 0:
                continue
            s = surplus[src]
            math = (f"{dest['name']}: {fmt_cents(f['due_cents'])} due - {fmt_cents(f['balance_cents'])} balance "
                    f"= {fmt_cents(f['shortfall_cents'])} short; {by_slug[src]['name']}: "
                    f"{fmt_cents(s['balance_cents'])} balance - {fmt_cents(s['own_due_cents'])} own due "
                    f"- {fmt_cents(s['buffer_cents'])} buffer = {fmt_cents(s['free'])} free")
            s["free"] -= amt
            need -= amt
            card = {"status": PREPARED, "from": src, "to": f["account"], "amount_cents": amt,
                    "reason": reason, "math": math, "due_by": by,
                    "text": f"Move {fmt_cents(amt)} from {by_slug[src]['name']} to {dest['name']}"
                            + (f" by {by}" if by else ""),
                    "how": f"Brandon does this himself in the {by_slug[src]['name']} app, if he chooses. "
                           "Genesis does not move money. Transfer timing and any fees are set by the "
                           "providers; check them in the app before sending."}
            if by_slug[src]["institution"] == "cash_app":
                card["fee_warning"] = CASH_APP_FEE_WARNING
            cards.append(card)
        if need > 0:
            cards.append({"status": "NO_SOURCE", "from": None, "to": f["account"], "amount_cents": need,
                          "reason": reason, "math": f"{dest['name']} shortfall {fmt_cents(f['shortfall_cents'])}; "
                                                    "no other account has known free surplus to cover the rest",
                          "due_by": by,
                          "text": f"No known surplus covers {fmt_cents(need)} for {dest['name']}",
                          "how": "Update balances, or record an outcome (arranged/disputed) on the item."})
    for i, c in enumerate(cards, 1):
        c["rank"] = i
    return cards

def daily_digest(snap: dict, today: date) -> dict:
    """Phase 2 Report: the daily digest as data -- balances, debits due in the
    next 7 days, uncovered bills, and the sweep cards awaiting Brandon's tap.
    Pure function of the snapshot; computing it writes nothing."""
    b = board(snap, today)
    return {"today": b["today"],
            "balances": [{"slug": a["slug"], "name": a["name"], "balance_cents": a["balance_cents"],
                          "balance_as_of": a["balance_as_of"],
                          "stale": a["slug"] in b["stale_balances"]} for a in b["accounts"]],
            "debits_due_7d": debit_watch(snap, today),
            "obligations_due_7d": b["due_window"],
            "uncovered": uncovered_items(snap, today),
            "deficits": b["deficits"],
            "sweeps": b["sweeps"],
            "sweep_cards_waiting": sum(1 for c in b["sweeps"] if c["status"] == PREPARED),
            "stale_balances": b["stale_balances"]}

def board(snap: dict, today: date, horizon: int = HORIZON_DAYS) -> dict:
    stale = []
    for a in snap["accounts"]:
        if a["kind"] == "asset" and a["balance_as_of"] and \
                (today - date.fromisoformat(a["balance_as_of"])).days > STALE_DAYS:
            stale.append(a["slug"])
    return {"today": today.isoformat(), "horizon_days": horizon,
            "accounts": snap["accounts"], "stale_balances": stale,
            "deficits": deficit_guard(snap, today, horizon),
            "bills": bill_calendar(snap, today),
            "due_window": due_window(snap, today),
            "debit_watch": debit_watch(snap, today),
            "sweeps": sweep_suggestions(snap, today, horizon)}
